source.citation: Schöler, A., Lothenbach, B., Winnefeld, F., Zajac, M. (2015). Hydration of quaternary Portland cement blends containing blast-furnace slag, siliceous fly ash and limestone powder. Cement and Concrete Composites 55, 374-382.
source.location: Tables 1 to 4 (pp. 375-376), Section 2 and Eqs. (3) and (4) (p. 376), Table 8 (p. 380)

transcription.from: the published article (PDF): the text layer, every table checked on the rendered page
transcription.note: Bound water and portlandite are given as a percentage of the dry sample weight at 500 °C: 'mdry solids = mass of dry paste corresponding to sample weight at 500 °C'; the portlandite from the weight loss of its dehydroxylation by the tangent method. In Table 1 'n.d.' (not determined) and the water-soluble Na2O of the slag, printed '<0.01', are null; the LOI is at 950 °C for OPC and BFS and at 1050 °C for FA and LS, and the 0.62 % of the slag is a gain on ignition, from the oxidation of its sulfide. Table 2 lists the phases of the four materials in two blocks; each row here names its material. The glass compositions of Table 3 are the authors' estimate, the water-soluble alkalis and the crystalline phases subtracted from the analysis.

tga_dry_solids_temperature.description: The temperature whose sample weight is the dry mass that bound water and portlandite are expressed against.

curing_temperature.description: The pastes were stored at 20 °C in sealed vessels.

so3_of_the_binder.description: The SO3 of every cement adjusted to 3 wt.% with anhydrite.

assumed_reaction_slag_glass.description: The long-term degree of reaction the authors assume for the amorphous part of the slag in their thermodynamic calculations, from 70 wt.% of the whole slag after one year in the literature they cite; an assumption of the paper, not a measurement of these pastes.

assumed_reaction_age.description: The age the assumed long-term degrees of reaction of the slag and the fly ash refer to: 'investigations of blast-furnace slag and fly ash blended Portland cements after one year of hydration'.

assumed_reaction_fly_ash_glass.description: The same for the amorphous part of the fly ash, from 30 wt.% of the whole fly ash.

oxides.location: Table 1, p. 375: chemical composition by XRF in mass percent, LOI, total, CO2 from TGA, water-soluble alkalis, Blaine fineness and density

phases.location: Table 2, p. 375: phase composition by XRD-Rietveld, mass percent

glass_composition.location: Table 3, p. 376: composition of the glass of the slag and the fly ash in mass percent, estimated by the authors

mixes.location: Table 4, p. 376: the quaternary cements, mass percent; the mix is named BFS-FA-LS

modeled_long_term.location: Table 7, p. 377: calculated by the authors (GEMS, Section 2.2) at the long-term degrees of reaction they assume (OPC 100 %, glass of the slag 71.1 %, glass of the fly ash 43.6 %), percent of the weight of the dry hydrates; the columns of the table are 30 and 20 % of slag with 20 and 30 % of fly ash, without limestone

tga.location: Table 8, p. 380: bound water excluding portlandite and portlandite from TGA, percent of the dry sample weight at 500 °C

notes: modeled_long_term: Table 7 is referred to the weight of the dry hydrates and Table 8 to the dry sample weight at 500 °C; the table does not say whether its bound water excludes that of portlandite, as Table 8's does, which at 1 % of portlandite is a quarter of a percent of water at most.
